notes: Exercise library. Schema in docs/CONTENT-SCHEMA.md. knee/back/sh = ok | caution | avoid for someone programming around meniscus tears, a lumbar disc, or a cranky shoulder. phase = earliest program phase (1 Rebuild, 2 Build, 3 Return).

exercises.name: Clamshell
cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent about 45°, heels together.
Keep the feet touching and lift the top knee — don't let the pelvis roll back.
2 s up, 2 s down. You should feel it on the side of the hip.
exercises.note: Add a mini band just above the knees once 20 per side feels easy.

exercises.name: Side-lying leg raise
cues: Bottom knee bent for balance, top leg straight and slightly behind your body.
Toes forward, lift leading with the heel to about 30–40°.
Lower slowly; keep the top hip stacked over the bottom one.
exercises.note: If you feel it in the front of the hip, bring the leg a little further back.

exercises.name: Side-lying front/back kick
cues: Top leg hovers at hip height.
Swing it forward to a comfortable stretch, then behind you.
Torso and pelvis stay still — only the leg moves.
exercises.note: Keep the back kick small; stop before the lower back arches.

exercises.name: Side-lying leg circles
cues: Top leg straight at hip height.
Small, controlled circles — 10 one way, 10 the other.
Hips stay stacked.

exercises.name: Side-lying inner-thigh lift
cues: Cross the top leg in front, foot on the floor or a pillow.
Lift the straight bottom leg a few inches, pause, lower slowly.
exercises.note: Adductor strength helps keep the knee tracking well.

exercises.name: Hip lift (glute bridge)
cues: Feet hip-width, heels about a foot from your glutes.
Exhale, ribs down, drive through the heels until knees, hips and shoulders line up.
Squeeze the glutes 2–3 s at the top; don't arch the lower back to get higher.
exercises.note: Strong hips take load off both the knees and the lower back.

exercises.name: Single-leg hip lift
cues: Same setup as the bridge, one foot lifted.
Keep the hips level as you rise — no tilting.
Pause at the top.

exercises.name: Terminal knee extension
cues: Anchor a band in front of you at knee height and loop it behind one knee.
From a slight bend, straighten the knee fully against the band.
Squeeze the thigh 2 s, release slowly.
exercises.note: Classic knee-rehab move: builds the quad with almost no stress on the meniscus.

exercises.name: Straight-leg raise
cues: Lie on your back, one knee bent, the other leg straight.
Tighten the straight leg's thigh, lift it to the height of the bent knee.
Lower over 3 s.
exercises.note: Keeping the other knee bent protects the lower back.

exercises.name: Mini-band lateral walk
cues: Band above the knees or at the ankles.
Quarter-squat stance, chest up.
Step sideways keeping tension; knees track over the toes.

exercises.name: Fire hydrant
cues: Hands and knees, spine neutral.
Lift one bent leg out to the side without tipping your torso.
Pause, lower slowly.
exercises.note: Pad under the knees; skip if kneeling bothers them.

exercises.name: Adductor squeeze
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, pillow or ball between the knees.
Squeeze 5–10 s, relax 5 s.

exercises.name: Quad set
cues: Sit with the leg straight, small towel roll under the knee.
Press the knee down by tightening the thigh; hold 5 s.
exercises.note: Good on flare days — keeps the quad switched on without moving the joint.

exercises.name: Tibialis raise
cues: Back against a wall, heels about a foot out.
Lift the toes toward your shins, lower slowly.
exercises.note: Strong shins help the knees absorb load on hills, stairs and slopes.

exercises.name: Lateral step-down
cues: Stand sideways on a low step (4–6 in).
Slowly bend the standing knee to tap the other heel on the floor.
Knee tracks over the second toe — no caving in.
exercises.note: Start very low; stop if you feel pinching or catching.

exercises.name: Hip hinge drill (dowel)
cues: Hold a broomstick along your spine: back of head, upper back and tailbone touching.
Soft knees, push the hips back until you feel the hamstrings.
Keep all three contact points the whole way.
exercises.note: Teaches the neutral-spine hinge that protects a disc in every deadlift, row and pick-up.

exercises.name: Bird dog
cues: Hands and knees, spine neutral.
Reach the opposite arm and leg long — no higher than your back.
Hold 8–10 s, return with control.
exercises.note: Part of the McGill Big 3 — the go-to disc-friendly core work. Pad under the knees.

exercises.name: McGill curl-up
cues: On your back, one knee bent, one leg straight, hands under the lower back.
Brace, then lift head and shoulders an inch or two as one unit.
Hold 8–10 s. Switch legs halfway.
exercises.note: The disc-friendly replacement for crunches: trains the abs without repeatedly bending the lower spine.

exercises.name: Box squat (bodyweight)
cues: Sit back to a box or chair at a height you can reach pain-free, touch lightly, stand up.
Knees track over the toes; weight through mid-foot.
Lower the box an inch at a time over weeks — only while it stays pain-free.
exercises.note: Depth is the dial for meniscus tears — deep, loaded knee bending is what irritates them. The box sets a safe floor.

exercises.name: Goblet box squat
cues: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest, elbows down.
Sit back to the box, touch, and stand — chest tall.
3 s down, 1 s up.
exercises.note: The front load keeps you upright, which is easier on the lower back than a bar across it.

exercises.name: TRX-assisted squat
cues: Hold the handles, lean back slightly, sit back to your pain-free depth.
Use the straps as much as you need; less assistance over time.

exercises.name: Air squat
cues: Feet shoulder-width, sit down between your heels.
Knees out over the toes, chest up.
Stand tall at the top.
exercises.note: Murph's biggest knee demand (300 of them). Build through box squats and keep depth pain-free.

exercises.name: Landmine squat
cues: Hold the bar end at your chest, lean into it slightly.
Sit back and down to pain-free depth, drive up.

exercises.name: Leg press (limited depth)
cues: Feet mid-platform, shoulder-width.
Lower only until the knees reach about 90°.
exercises.note: Stop before your hips curl off the seat — that tuck is hard on discs.

exercises.name: Barbell box squat
cues: Bar on the upper back, brace hard.
Sit back to the box, pause without relaxing, drive up.
Box height = your pain-free depth.
exercises.note: The bridge from goblet squats back to the barbell.

exercises.name: Back squat
cues: Big breath, brace, unrack.
Sit down between the heels to the depth you own pain-free.
No bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.note: Big 4 lift. A box at your pain-free depth is fine forever.

exercises.name: Front squat
cues: Bar on the front of the shoulders, elbows high.
Stay upright, sit straight down to pain-free depth.
exercises.note: More upright than a back squat (friendlier to the back) but asks for more knee bend.

exercises.name: Step-up (low)
cues: 6–8 in step, whole foot on it.
Drive through the heel to stand tall; don't push off the bottom foot.
Lower slowly (3 s).

exercises.name: Split squat (partial range)
cues: Long split stance, hold a wall or chair.
Drop straight down only as far as is pain-free — the back knee doesn't need to touch.
Front knee stays over the foot, not caving in.

exercises.name: TRX-assisted split squat
cues: Hold the handles for balance and assistance.
Lower to pain-free depth, drive up through the front heel.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge (short)
cues: Step back, lower under control to pain-free depth.
Push through the front heel to return.
exercises.note: Reverse lunges are kinder to knees than forward lunges. Add dumbbells when easy.

exercises.name: Single-leg sit-to-stand
cues: Sit on a box on one leg (other foot hovering), stand up.
Use a high box first; control the way down.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
cues: Rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough out that the shin stays fairly vertical.
Keep the range short and pain-free.
exercises.note: Deep front-knee bend — the last single-leg progression, not the first.

exercises.name: Kettlebell deadlift (elevated)
cues: Set the bell on a step or blocks so the handle is around mid-shin.
Hips back, spine long, lats tight, then drive the floor away.
Stop the moment the lower back wants to round.
exercises.note: Elevating the weight shortens the range so you learn to hinge with a neutral spine — the key disc skill.

exercises.name: Band pull-through
cues: Band anchored low behind you, between your legs.
Hinge back with a flat back, then snap the hips forward and squeeze.

exercises.name: Cable pull-through
cues: Rope on a low pulley between the legs.
Hinge back with a flat back, drive the hips through and squeeze.

exercises.name: Single-leg RDL (supported)
cues: Hold a wall or chair with one hand.
Hinge at the hip; the back leg lifts as the torso tips. Keep hips square.
Soft standing knee, spine long.
exercises.note: Add a light dumbbell in the free hand later.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Dumbbells in front of the thighs, soft knees.
Push the hips back, weights slide down the legs.
Stop at mid-shin or when the back wants to round.

exercises.name: 45° back extension
cues: Hip crease at the edge of the pad.
Hinge down with a neutral spine, rise until your body is straight — not past it.

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift (high handles)
cues: Stand in the center, grab the high handles.
Hips back, chest up, brace — push the floor away.
Lock out with glutes, not by leaning back.
exercises.note: The most back-friendly way to deadlift heavy: the load stays in line with your body.

exercises.name: Deadlift (conventional)
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins to the bar, flat back.
Pull the slack out, brace, push the floor away.
Reset each rep — no bouncing.
exercises.note: Big 4 lift. Pull from blocks first if the floor forces your back to round.

exercises.name: Deadlift (sumo)
cues: Wide stance, toes out, hands inside the knees.
Knees out, chest up, push the floor apart.
exercises.note: More upright torso than conventional — many lifters with back history prefer it.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Start standing, soft knees.
Hips back, bar close to the legs, stop before the back rounds.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
cues: Upper back on a bench, feet flat, load (band, dumbbell or bar) across the hips.
Tuck the ribs, drive up until the torso is level; squeeze 1–2 s.
Don't finish by arching the lower back.
exercises.note: Big glute strength with no spinal load and little knee bend.

exercises.name: Calf raise
cues: Rise onto the balls of the feet, pause, lower over 3 s.
Hold a wall; progress to single-leg, then off a step.

exercises.name: TRX hamstring curl
cues: Heels in the foot cradles, hips lifted.
Curl the heels in keeping hips high; extend slowly.
exercises.note: Knee bending under load — keep it smooth and stop short of any pinch behind the knee.

exercises.name: Stability-ball hamstring curl
cues: Heels on the ball, hips up.
Roll the ball in, keep hips high, roll out slowly.

exercises.name: Towel hamstring curl
cues: Heels on a towel on a smooth floor, hips up.
Slide the heels in, then out slowly — the out is the hard part.

exercises.name: Leg curl (machine)
cues: Pad just above the heels.
Curl smoothly; limit the range if the back of the knee pinches.

exercises.name: Nordic curl (assisted)
cues: Kneel with the ankles anchored, body straight.
Lower as slowly as you can, catch yourself, push back up.
exercises.note: Very demanding — use a band or partial range. Kneeling needs a thick pad.

exercises.name: Leg extension (partial range)
cues: Light weight, roughly 90° to 30° of knee bend.
Slow and smooth.
exercises.note: Skip it if it aggravates the knees — the Spanish squat does the same job.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
cues: Hands on a bench, counter or sturdy chair.
One straight line — glutes squeezed, ribs down.
Chest to the edge, press away.
exercises.note: Lower the surface over time until you're on the floor.

exercises.name: Push-up
cues: Hands just outside the shoulders, body straight.
Elbows about 45° from your sides.
Chest to a fist from the floor, then press.
exercises.note: Don't let the hips sag — a sagging plank arches the lower back.

exercises.name: Close-grip push-up
cues: Hands under the shoulders, elbows tight to the ribs.
Straight body; hands on a bench to make it easier.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
cues: Lie on the floor, knees bent, dumbbells over the chest.
Lower until the upper arms touch the floor, pause, press.
exercises.note: The floor limits range — easy on the shoulders and a great home bench substitute.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
cues: Shoulder blades pinched, feet planted.
Lower to chest level with elbows ~45°, press up and slightly in.

exercises.name: Bench press
cues: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched.
Lower to the lower chest, touch, press back over the shoulders.
exercises.note: Big 4 lift. If leg drive or a big arch bothers your back, put your feet up on the bench.

exercises.name: TRX chest press
cues: Face away from the anchor, arms straight out, lean in.
Lower the chest between the handles, press back — plank body.

exercises.name: Band chest press
cues: Band anchored behind you at chest height.
Staggered stance, press forward, return slowly.

exercises.name: Chest press (machine)
cues: Handles at mid-chest.
Press out, return under control.

exercises.name: Dips
cues: Shoulders down, slight forward lean.
Lower to about 90° at the elbow, press up.
exercises.note: Skip if the shoulders complain.

exercises.name: Bench dip
cues: Hands on a chair or bench behind you, knees bent.
Lower a short way (elbows to ~90° max), shoulders down, press up.
exercises.note: Travel-friendly triceps work. Keep it shallow.

exercises.name: Close-grip bench press
cues: Hands shoulder-width, elbows tucked.
Lower to the lower chest, press.

exercises.name: Landmine press
cues: Hold the bar end at the shoulder, staggered stance.
Press up and forward along the bar's arc, ribs down.
exercises.note: The angled press is easy on shoulders and doesn't invite a lower-back arch.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Bench upright, back supported.
Press overhead without arching away from the pad.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell press
cues: Glutes squeezed, ribs down.
Press overhead — no leaning back.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling dumbbell press
cues: One knee down (padded), same-side hand presses.
Squeeze the down-side glute — it stops the back arching.

exercises.name: Band overhead press
cues: Stand on the band, handles at the shoulders.
Press overhead, ribs down.

exercises.name: Pike push-up
cues: Hips high, hands and feet on the floor (inverted V).
Lower the head toward the floor between the hands, press back.

exercises.name: Shoulder press (machine)
cues: Back against the pad.
Press up, lower under control.

exercises.name: Overhead press
cues: Bar on the front delts, grip just outside the shoulders.
Glutes tight, ribs down, press and move the head through.
exercises.note: Big 4 lift. Leaning back to finish the press shifts load onto the lower back.

exercises.name: TRX row
cues: Walk the feet forward to set the angle — steeper is harder.
Body straight, pull the handles to your ribs, squeeze the shoulder blades.
Lower with control.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
cues: Chest on an incline bench.
Row the dumbbells to the hips, pause, lower slowly.
exercises.note: The bench takes the lower back out of it entirely.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
cues: One hand on a bench, feet staggered on the floor (no knee on the bench).
Flat back; pull the dumbbell to your hip pocket.

exercises.name: Band row
cues: Band anchored at chest height.
Stand tall, pull the elbows back, squeeze the shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
cues: Sit tall; don't round forward to reach the handle.
Pull to the belly, squeeze, return slowly.

exercises.name: Row (machine)
cues: Chest on the pad.
Pull the elbows back, pause, return.

exercises.name: Inverted row
cues: Bar set in a rack at waist height.
Hang under it, body straight, pull the chest to the bar.

exercises.name: Seal row
cues: Lie face-down on a high bench.
Row the bar to the bench, lower fully.

exercises.name: Barbell row
cues: Hinge to ~45°, flat back.
Row to the lower ribs, lower under control.
exercises.note: Hinged rowing loads the lower back — earn it with chest-supported rows first.

exercises.name: Door-frame row
cues: Grip a sturdy door frame with one hand, feet close to it.
Lean back with a straight arm, then pull yourself in.
exercises.note: Zero-equipment hotel row. Use a solid frame, never the door itself.

exercises.name: Chin-up
cues: Palms facing you, shoulder-width.
Pull the chest toward the bar, lower all the way.
exercises.note: More biceps than a pull-up. Hanging also gently decompresses the spine.

exercises.name: Pull-up
cues: Palms away, a bit wider than the shoulders.
Shoulders down first, then pull the chin over the bar.
No kipping.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
cues: Loop a band over the bar, foot or knee in the loop.
Full hang to chin over; use lighter bands over time.

exercises.name: Pull-up negative
cues: Step up to the top position (chin over the bar).
Lower yourself over 3–5 s.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
cues: Thighs under the pad, chest up.
Pull the bar to the upper chest, elbows down and back.

exercises.name: TRX-assisted pull-up
cues: Straps short, sit under the handles.
Pull the chest up to the hands, using the legs as little as possible.

exercises.name: Band lat pulldown
cues: Anchor the band high; sit or stand.
Pull the elbows down to the ribs.

exercises.name: Straight-arm pulldown
cues: Anchor high, arms straight.
Sweep the hands down to the thighs, ribs down.

exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
cues: Hang with straight arms.
Pull the shoulder blades down and together without bending the elbows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell curl
cues: Elbows pinned at your sides.
Curl up, squeeze, lower over 2–3 s.
exercises.note: No swinging — if you have to lean back, the weight is too heavy and your back pays for it.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
cues: Palms facing each other.
Curl without swinging; control the way down.
exercises.note: Builds the brachialis — the muscle that pushes the biceps up and makes the arm look thicker.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell curl
cues: Bench at ~45°, arms hanging behind you.
Curl without letting the elbows drift forward.
exercises.note: The stretched start position hits the long head of the biceps (the peak).

exercises.name: Concentration curl
cues: Seated, elbow braced on the inner thigh.
Curl up, squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: TRX biceps curl
cues: Face the anchor, palms up, lean back with straight arms.
Curl the hands toward the forehead keeping elbows high; body straight.

exercises.name: Band curl
cues: Stand on the band.
Curl up, pause, lower slowly — fight the band on the way down.

exercises.name: EZ-bar curl
cues: Shoulder-width grip, elbows pinned.
Glutes squeezed so you can't lean back.

exercises.name: Cable curl
cues: Low pulley, elbows at your sides.
Constant tension — no rest at the bottom.

exercises.name: Backpack curl
cues: Load a backpack (water bottles, books) and hold it by the top handle or straps.
Elbows pinned, curl slowly, lower over 3 s.
exercises.note: Hotel-room biceps. Go slow — the tempo makes a light load count.

exercises.name: Self-resisted towel curl
cues: Step on the middle of a towel with one foot, hold both ends.
Curl up while pressing down with the foot to make it hard; resist on the way down too.

exercises.name: Preacher curl (machine)
cues: Armpits snug to the pad.
Don't fully relax at the bottom.

exercises.name: Band triceps pushdown
cues: Anchor the band high.
Elbows pinned, push down to full lockout, squeeze.

exercises.name: Cable triceps pushdown
cues: Rope or bar, elbows at your sides.
Push to lockout, spread the rope at the bottom.

exercises.name: TRX triceps extension
cues: Face away from the anchor, arms out, lean in.
Bend only the elbows to bring hands toward the forehead, then extend.

exercises.name: Dumbbell skull crusher
cues: On the floor or a bench, dumbbells over the shoulders, palms facing.
Lower beside the head bending only the elbows, extend.

exercises.name: Seated overhead triceps extension
cues: Seated with back support, one dumbbell held overhead in both hands.
Lower behind the head, extend — don't arch.
exercises.note: Overhead work stretches the long head of the triceps — most of the arm's back-side mass.

exercises.name: Triceps kickback
cues: One hand on a bench, flat back.
Upper arm still, extend the elbow fully, squeeze.

exercises.name: Band pull-apart
cues: Arms straight in front, band at shoulder width.
Pull apart to the chest, squeeze the shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Face pull
cues: Anchor at face height.
Pull toward the eyes, elbows high, rotate the hands back.

exercises.name: TRX Y raise
cues: Face the anchor, lean back, arms straight.
Raise the arms into a Y overhead, body straight.

exercises.name: TRX reverse fly (T)
cues: Face the anchor, arms straight.
Open the arms out to a T, squeeze the upper back.

exercises.name: TRX face pull
cues: Palms down, pull the handles toward the forehead, elbows high and wide.

exercises.name: Chest-supported reverse fly
cues: Chest on an incline bench, light dumbbells.
Sweep the arms out wide, pinkies up, pause.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W
cues: Face down, forehead on a towel.
Lift the arms into Y, then T, then W — a small chest lift is fine.
exercises.note: Gentle extension is usually fine for disc issues; skip it if it sends symptoms down a leg.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides.
Shrug straight up, pause 1 s, lower.

exercises.name: Dead bug
cues: On your back, arms up, knees over hips.
Ribs down, lower back quietly against the floor.
Extend the opposite arm and leg slowly, return, switch.

exercises.name: TRX fallout
cues: Face away from the anchor, arms straight, lean in from a steep angle.
Let the arms rise overhead while the body stays rigid, pull back.
exercises.note: Only as far as you can go without the lower back sagging.

exercises.name: TRX body saw
cues: Forearm plank with the feet in the cradles.
Rock the body back and forward a few inches — no sagging.

exercises.name: Ab-wheel rollout (kneeling)
cues: Kneel on a thick pad, ribs down, glutes tight.
Roll out only as far as you can keep the back from sagging, pull back.

exercises.name: Stir the pot
cues: Forearm plank on a stability ball.
Draw small circles with the forearms, body rigid.

exercises.name: Pallof press
cues: Stand side-on to the anchor, hands at the chest.
Press straight out and resist the twist, return.
exercises.note: Anti-rotation core — trains the obliques the disc-safe way (instead of twists).

exercises.name: Half-kneeling chop
cues: One knee down (padded), band anchored high to one side.
Pull across and down, torso stays square — the arms move, the spine doesn't.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
cues: Dead hang, shoulders active.
Raise the knees to hip height with a small pelvic tuck, lower slowly. No swinging.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch (small)
cues: On your back, knees bent up.
Curl the pelvis a few inches off the floor, lower slowly — no rocking.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
cues: Heavy weight in one hand only.
Walk tall — don't lean toward or away from the weight.
exercises.note: Works the side abs by resisting the lean. On the road, your actual suitcase works.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
cues: Heavy weight in each hand, stand tall, shoulders down.
Short, quick steps; breathe behind the brace.

exercises.name: Goblet carry
cues: Hold the weight at the chest.
Walk tall; ribs down, don't lean back.

exercises.name: Bear-hug carry
cues: Hug a sandbag (or any awkward heavy object) high on the chest.
Stand tall and walk — don't lean back to balance it.
exercises.note: The closest training there is for carrying a person.

exercises.name: Zercher carry
cues: Bar in the crook of the elbows (pad it), unrack from pins.
Stand tall and walk.

exercises.name: Loaded backpack walk
cues: Backpack loaded with books or water bottles, straps snug.
Walk tall for time.

exercises.name: Plank
cues: Forearms under the shoulders, body straight.
Squeeze glutes and quads, ribs down, breathe.
exercises.note: Quality over time: end the set when the hips start to sag.

exercises.name: Side plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, hips up in a straight line.
Start from the knees if needed.
exercises.note: McGill Big 3.

exercises.name: Bear plank
cues: Hands and knees, then lift the knees an inch off the floor.
Flat back, breathe.

exercises.name: Hollow hold
cues: On your back, lower back pressed down, arms and legs lifted.
Tuck the knees to make it easier.
exercises.note: Only as low as you can keep the lower back glued down.

exercises.name: Dead bug hold
cues: Dead bug position, extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Hold with the lower back quiet; switch halfway.

exercises.name: Pallof hold
cues: Pallof press position, arms extended.
Hold still against the pull.

exercises.name: Bird dog hold
cues: Opposite arm and leg long, hold.
Hips level, no rotation.

exercises.name: Copenhagen plank (short lever)
cues: Side plank with the top knee resting on a bench, bottom leg hanging.
Lift the hips and hold.
exercises.note: Short lever only (knee on the bench) — the ankle-on-bench version stresses the knee joint.

exercises.name: Glute bridge hold
cues: Top of the bridge, ribs down.
Squeeze the glutes the whole time.

exercises.name: Single-leg bridge hold
cues: One foot down, hips level at the top.
Hold without the hips dropping.

exercises.name: Spanish squat hold
cues: Loop a heavy band around a sturdy post and behind both knees.
Sit back into the band, shins vertical, to a quarter-to-half squat.
Hold.
exercises.note: A knee-friendly quad builder often used to calm cranky knees. Keep it shallow.

exercises.name: Wall sit (high)
cues: Back flat against the wall, feet out in front.
Slide down only until the knees bend 45–60° — hips well above knees.
Press the whole foot into the floor.
exercises.note: Quad work with little meniscus stress. Go deeper only when this is easy and pain-free.

exercises.name: Wall sit (parallel)
cues: Thighs toward parallel, knees over the ankles.
Only if the high version is pain-free.

exercises.name: Split squat hold
cues: Split stance, lower to a pain-free depth and hold.
Hold a wall for balance.

exercises.name: Dead hang
cues: Full grip, arms straight, relax the legs.
Let the spine lengthen; breathe.
exercises.note: Hanging gently decompresses the spine — a nice one for disc issues. Step down, don't drop.

exercises.name: Flexed-arm hang
cues: Chin-up grip, start at the top (step up to it).
Hold the chin over the bar as long as you can.

exercises.name: Biceps 90° hold
cues: Curl to a 90° elbow and hold there — dumbbell, band, loaded bag, or a towel under your foot pulled as hard as you can.
Elbows at your sides; squeeze the biceps hard.

exercises.name: Farmer hold
cues: Heavy weight in each hand, stand tall.
Hold; shoulders down and back.

exercises.name: Door-frame lat hang
cues: Grip a sturdy door frame high with both hands.
Sit the hips back and let the arms and lats stretch; squeeze the grip.
exercises.note: No-bar substitute for hanging on the road.

exercises.name: Foam roll: quads
cues: Face down, roller under the thighs.
Roll slowly from hip to just above the kneecap.
exercises.note: Stay off the knee joint itself.

exercises.name: Foam roll: outer thigh
cues: Side-lying at a 45° angle — outer quad, not straight on the IT band.
Slow passes, pause on tender spots.
exercises.note: Stop a hand's width above the knee.

exercises.name: Foam roll: glutes
cues: Sit on the roller, cross one ankle over the other knee.
Lean toward the crossed side and roll slowly.

exercises.name: Foam roll: hamstrings
cues: Roller under the thighs, hands behind you.
Roll from the glute crease to above the knee.

exercises.name: Foam roll: calves
cues: Roller under one calf, other leg crossed on top for pressure.
Turn the foot in and out to find spots.

exercises.name: Foam roll: upper back
cues: Roller across the upper back, hands supporting the head.
Roll between the shoulder blades; pause and gently extend over it.
exercises.note: Upper back only. Never foam-roll the lower back.

exercises.name: Foam roll: lats
cues: Side-lying, roller under the armpit, arm overhead.
Roll down the side of the back a few inches.

exercises.name: Ball release: glute
cues: Sit on a lacrosse ball on one glute (or lean against a wall).
Find a tender spot, breathe, let it melt 20–30 s.

exercises.name: Ball release: chest
cues: Ball between the chest (below the collarbone) and a wall.
Lean in, small circles, slide the arm up and down.

exercises.name: Ball roll: foot
cues: Standing, roll the arch of the foot over the ball.
Heel to toes, pressure as tolerated.

exercises.name: Ball release: upper back
cues: Ball between the shoulder blade and spine, against a wall.
Small squats to roll it around; cross the arm over the chest.

exercises.name: Standing hip flexor stretch
cues: Split stance, back heel up.
Tuck the tailbone and squeeze the back-leg glute until the front of the hip stretches.
Don't lean or arch.
exercises.note: Tight hip flexors pull on the lower back; this version needs no kneeling.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: One knee down on a thick pad.
Tuck the pelvis, squeeze the glute, shift forward slightly.

exercises.name: Strap hamstring stretch
cues: On your back, strap around one foot, other leg bent or flat.
Raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch; relax.
exercises.note: Lying down keeps the spine neutral — the disc-safe hamstring stretch.

exercises.name: Supine figure-4 stretch
cues: On your back, cross one ankle over the other knee.
Pull the bottom thigh toward you until the glute stretches.
exercises.note: Use this instead of pigeon pose. Stop if you feel it in the knee rather than the hip.

exercises.name: Seated figure-4 stretch
cues: Sit tall on a chair, ankle over the opposite knee.
Hinge forward with a flat back until the glute stretches.

exercises.name: Doorway chest stretch
cues: Forearm on the door frame, elbow at shoulder height.
Step through gently until the chest stretches.

exercises.name: Lat stretch
cues: Hands on a counter or chair back, arms straight.
Walk back and sink the hips back, chest toward the floor, back flat.

exercises.name: Wall calf stretch
cues: Hands on the wall, one leg back, heel down.
Lean in until the calf stretches; bend the back knee slightly for the lower calf.

exercises.name: Open book
cues: Side-lying, knees bent and stacked, arms out in front.
Open the top arm across to the other side, following it with your eyes.
Hips stay put — the movement is in the upper back.

exercises.name: Cat-cow
cues: Hands and knees.
Slowly round, then gently arch, staying in a pain-free range.
exercises.note: Motion, not a stretch — think gentle flossing for the spine. Pad the knees.

exercises.name: Thread the needle
cues: Hands and knees, slide one arm under the other.
Rest the shoulder down, then open that arm to the ceiling.

exercises.name: Sphinx
cues: Face down, prop on the forearms, elbows under the shoulders.
Let the belly soften; breathe.
exercises.note: Gentle extension often eases disc irritation. If it sends pain down a leg, stop.

exercises.name: Prone press-up
cues: Face down, hands under the shoulders.
Press the chest up, hips stay down and relaxed.
exercises.note: Only if your PT uses extension exercises with you. Stop if symptoms move further down the leg.

exercises.name: Child's pose (supported)
cues: Wide knees, pillow between the calves and thighs to limit the bend.
Arms long, breathe into the back.
exercises.note: Deep knee bend — skip it if the knees complain.

exercises.name: Wall angel
cues: Back, head and arms against the wall, ribs down.
Slide the arms up and down like a snow angel.

exercises.name: Neck stretch
cues: Ear toward shoulder, opposite hand reaching down.
Gentle — no pulling.

exercises.name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility
cues: Foot a few inches from the wall.
Drive the knee forward to touch the wall, heel down.

exercises.name: Hip circles (CARs)
cues: Stand tall holding a wall.
Draw the biggest slow circle you can with the knee, torso still.

exercises.name: Arm circles
cues: Small to big circles, forward then back.

exercises.name: Leg swings
cues: Hold a wall; swing one leg front to back, then side to side.
Relaxed, growing range.

exercises.name: Knee to chest
cues: On your back, hug one knee in gently.
exercises.note: Flexion — some discs like it, some don't. Follow your symptoms.

exercises.name: Standing back bend (gentle)
cues: Hands on the lower back, feet hip-width.
Lean back gently a few inches, return.
exercises.note: A classic reset after long sitting (flights, drives). Only if it feels good.

exercises.name: Seated ankle pumps & glute squeezes
cues: In your seat: point and flex the feet 20 times.
Squeeze the glutes 5 s, 10 times.
exercises.note: Keeps blood moving on long flights.

exercises.name: Mountain pose
cues: Feet hip-width, soft knees (not locked).
Tall through the crown, shoulders down, breathe.

exercises.name: Standing side bend
cues: Arms overhead, reach up and over to one side.
Keep the chest open — lengthen, don't crunch.

exercises.name: Half lift (flat back)
cues: Hinge forward with bent knees, hands on the shins or blocks.
Spine long and flat — no rounding.
exercises.note: Replaces the full rounded forward fold.

exercises.name: Downward dog (bent knees)
cues: Hands wide, hips high, knees generously bent.
Push the floor away; lengthen the spine before the legs.
exercises.note: Bent knees keep the lower back from rounding.

exercises.name: Low cobra
cues: Face down, hands by the ribs.
Lift the chest a few inches with the back muscles, elbows hugged in.

exercises.name: Warrior II (short stance)
cues: Shorter stance than usual; front knee over the ankle, tracking the middle toes.
Bend no deeper than 90° — less is fine.

exercises.name: Warrior I (short stance)
cues: Short stance, back heel lifted if the knee or hip complains.
Tuck the tailbone slightly; reach up.

exercises.name: Triangle (supported)
cues: Hand on a block or the shin, not the floor.
Micro-bend the front knee — never lock or hyperextend it.
Long spine, open chest.

exercises.name: Low lunge (padded)
cues: Back knee on a thick pad, front knee over the ankle.
Tuck the pelvis and lift the chest; don't sink into the lower back.

exercises.name: Tree pose
cues: Foot on the ankle or calf — never press on the knee.
Hands at the chest or overhead; steady gaze.

exercises.name: Chair pose (shallow)
cues: Sit back a little, weight in the heels.
Keep it shallow; arms up, ribs down.

exercises.name: Locust (gentle)
cues: Face down, arms by your sides.
Lengthen and lift the chest and legs a few inches.

exercises.name: Bridge pose
cues: Feet under the knees, lift the hips.
Glutes do the work — don't push the ribs up.

exercises.name: Supine twist (gentle)
cues: On your back, knees bent, let them drop to one side onto a pillow.
Small range; shoulders stay down.
exercises.note: Rotation — keep it small and pillow-supported; skip if the back grumbles.

exercises.name: Reclined bound angle (propped)
cues: On your back, soles together, knees apart.
Pillows or blocks under both knees so nothing strains.

exercises.name: Legs up the wall
cues: Hips near the wall, legs resting up it.
Arms out, breathe slow.

exercises.name: Savasana
cues: On your back, pillow under the knees to ease the lower back.
Let everything go heavy.

exercises.name: Crunch / sit-up
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Repeated loaded spinal flexion is the classic disc aggravator. Use McGill curl-ups, dead bugs and planks — your abs still get the work.

exercises.name: Russian twist
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Flexion plus rotation under load is the worst combo for discs. Pallof presses and side planks train the obliques safely.

exercises.name: Good morning
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Long lever on the lower back with a bar on it. The trap-bar and RDL do the job with less risk.

exercises.name: Jump squat / box jump
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Landing impact on bent knees is rough on meniscus tears. Revisit only once your PT clears jumping.

exercises.name: Deep squat hold
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Resting at the bottom of a deep squat pinches the back of the meniscus.

exercises.name: Hero pose / sitting on heels
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Full knee flexion under bodyweight. Use a chair or supported child's pose instead.

exercises.name: Pigeon pose
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Twists the front knee. Supine figure-4 stretches the same glute without the torque.

exercises.name: Seated forward fold
cues: Not programmed.
exercises.note: Rounded, loaded flexion stretches the back of the disc. The strap hamstring stretch lying down is the swap.

exercises.name: Fighting stance & guard
cues: Staggered stance, weight on the balls of the feet, knees soft.
Hands up, elbows in, chin down.

exercises.name: Footwork: forward & back
cues: Push off the back foot to move forward, front foot to move back.
Short steps; never cross or bring the feet together.

exercises.name: Footwork: lateral
cues: Step with the foot nearest the direction, the other follows.
Stay in stance the whole time.

exercises.name: Footwork: angles & circling
cues: Step off-line at 45°, then re-square.
Turn by stepping — let the heel pivot freely.
exercises.note: Knee rule: never twist on a planted, bent knee. Light feet, pivot on the ball of the foot.

exercises.name: Straight punches
cues: Punch straight from the guard, rotate the hips, return to guard.
Let the rear heel turn out so the knee isn't torqued.

exercises.name: Palm-heel strikes
cues: Fingers back, strike with the heel of the palm.
Same body mechanics as the straight punch.

exercises.name: Hammerfists
cues: Strike with the meaty bottom of the fist — forward, down and to the side.

exercises.name: Elbow strikes
cues: Horizontal, upward and back elbows.
Turn the hips into each; keep the other hand guarding.

exercises.name: Knee strikes
cues: Drive the knee up and forward with the hips.
Supporting knee soft; come up on the ball of the foot.
exercises.note: The striking knee is fine; watch the standing one — no twisting on it.

exercises.name: Front kick (groin)
cues: Lift the knee, snap the shin up, strike with the instep.
Don't lock the kicking knee at full extension.

exercises.name: Defensive front kick
cues: Chamber the knee, push through with the ball of the foot.
Stay upright — don't lean way back.

exercises.name: 360° defense drill
cues: Cycle through the seven outside-defense positions, forearm bent at 90°.
Burst in with a counter-punch after each.

exercises.name: Choke-release drill
cues: Front, side and rear choke releases (pluck), shadowed solo or with a partner.
Pluck, counter, disengage.

exercises.name: Shadowboxing
cues: Move and strike: straights, palm heels, hammerfists, elbows.
Add 360° defenses and bursts. Keep the hands up.
exercises.note: Knee rule: pivot on the ball of the foot, never twist a planted bent knee.

exercises.name: Stationary shadowboxing
cues: Feet stay planted in stance; all the work is upper body.
Fast hands, tight guard.
exercises.note: Knee-flare version.

exercises.name: Heavy bag rounds
cues: Wrap your hands.
Combos in bursts, move around the bag between them.

exercises.name: Tactical get-up
cues: From sitting: post a hand, lift the hips, sweep the leg back to stance.
Hand up to guard the whole time.

exercises.name: Back breakfall
cues: Only on mats with a coach.
exercises.note: Falls load the lower back — skip until your doctor or PT clears it.

exercises.name: Incline burpee (no jump)
cues: Hands on a bench or chair, step back to a plank, push-up optional.
Step in, stand tall. No jump.
exercises.note: Knee- and back-friendly swap for burpees.

exercises.name: Slow mountain climbers
cues: Plank position, drive one knee toward the chest, return.
Controlled pace; hands on a bench to make it easier.

exercises.name: Step jacks
cues: Step one foot out as the arms go up, return, alternate.
Low-impact jumping jack.

exercises.name: Bear crawl
cues: Hands and feet, knees hovering an inch up.
Crawl forward and back; flat back, small steps.

exercises.name: Plank shoulder taps
cues: High plank, feet wide.
Tap the opposite shoulder without the hips rocking.

exercises.name: Straight-punch sprint
cues: Fast alternating straight punches for the interval.
Stay in stance, hands snap back.

exercises.name: Band-resisted punches
cues: Band anchored behind you at shoulder height.
Punch straight out against it, return to guard.

exercises.name: Skater step (no jump)
cues: Step wide to one side, sweep the other foot behind.
Soft knees, stay low but pain-free.

exercises.name: Jump rope
cues: Tiny hops on the balls of the feet.
exercises.note: Impact — wait until your PT clears hopping.

exercises.name: Stationary bike
cues: Seat height: a slight bend (about 25–35°) at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Raise the handlebars if your back complains.
exercises.note: A seat that's too low means deep knee bends thousands of times — set it right.

exercises.name: Walk
cues: Tall posture, arms swinging.
Brisk enough to breathe a little harder.
exercises.note: Walking is one of the best things you can do for a disc.

exercises.name: Incline treadmill walk
cues: Moderate incline, don't hold the rails.
Uphill is easier on the knees than downhill.

exercises.name: Run
cues: Short, quick steps landing under the hips.
Easy pace — you should be able to talk.

exercises.name: Walk-run intervals
cues: Alternate easy running and walking.
Stop if the knee aches during or swells after.

exercises.name: Elliptical
cues: Stand tall, light hands.
Low-impact running substitute.

exercises.name: Rower
cues: Legs, then body, then arms — reverse on the way back.
Don't round the lower back at the catch.

exercises.name: Swim
cues: Freestyle or backstroke.
exercises.note: Skip the breaststroke whip kick — it twists the knees.

exercises.name: Stair climber
cues: Whole foot on each step, upright.

exercises.name: Hike
cues: Poles take a lot of load off the knees on descents.
